candidates.exact_span: a.   Pollutant Table (2 or 3) appropriate for permittee's land app lication practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Table 2 (loading-rate limits) or Table 3 (concentration criteria) governs depends on which table is 'appropriate' for the permittee's land application practices; a different reading changes which enforceable numeric limits apply (A) and which pollutant framework must be reported (B).

candidates.exact_span: b.   The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable monitoring frequency is cross-referenced to Element 1, Section I.C. and is permittee-specific; interpreting which frequency 'applies' changes which monitoring obligations were required in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: c.   Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) results (Pass/Fail).
candidates.computation_change_reason: TCLP is reported as Pass/Fail rather than a numeric concentration; interpreting this as an enforceable numeric limit versus report-only or qualitative compliance affects limit-exceedance analysis (A), whether TCLP monitoring was an obligation (B), and how missing or non-numeric TCLP evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: d.   The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) as well as the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/K g) listed in Table 3 found in Element 1, Section III, or the applicable pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above if it exceeds 90% of the limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This item ties reported Table 1 monthly-average concentrations to either Table 3 concentration criteria or Table 2 loading-rate limits, but only when results exceed 90% of the limit; different readings of 'monthly average,' which table applies, and the 90% trigger change which numeric limits are enforceable for comparison (A), when heightened reporting/monitoring is required (B), and whether absent data reflects a non-triggered state versus missing required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: e.   Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Class A versus Class B pathogen reduction determines eligibility for the Section III Table 3 regime and associated conditions; misclassifying the achieved class changes which pollutant limits and requirements apply (A) and which pathogen-related monitoring/reporting obligations attach (B).

candidates.exact_span: f.   Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met. If Class B sludge, include information on how site restrictions were met in the DMR comment section or attach a separate sheet to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Section I.B.3 alternative is used, and for Class B whether site-restriction evidence is in DMR comments versus an attachment, affects what monitoring/reporting was required (B) and how to classify periods where that evidence is absent or ambiguous (C).

candidates.exact_span: g.   Vector attraction reduction alternative used as listed in Section I.B.4. h.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable vector-attraction alternative under Section I.B.4.h is cross-referenced rather than stated here; interpreting which alternative applies changes which vector-attraction monitoring/reporting obligations were in force.

candidates.exact_span: k.   The certification statement listed in 503.17(a)(4)(i)(B) or 503.17(a)(5)(i)(B) whichever applies to the permittees sludge treatment activities shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Two distinct 503.17 certification provisions are invoked with a 'whichever applies' selector tied to treatment activities; different interpretations of which provision applies change the required certification evidence (B) and whether a missing certification is a documented no-data state or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: l.   When the amount of any pollutant applied to the land exceeds 90% of the cumulative pollutant loading rate for that pollutant, as described in Table 2, the permittee shall report the following information as an attachment to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 90%-of-cumulative-loading-rate threshold activates additional site-specific reporting tied to Table 2; interpreting whether cumulative applications crossed 90% changes proximity-to-limit analysis (A), triggers supplemental monitoring/reporting duties (B), and determines whether missing site-level data reflects a non-applicable condition or missing required evidence (C).
